Who pays, and who carries the risk.
Blue steps are paid by the seller, yellow steps by the buyer. Costs move to the buyer at a different point under each rule.
The red line shows the moment loss or damage stops being the seller’s problem. Under C rules this is long before the cost split.
Export clearance sits with the seller under every rule except EXW. Import clearance sits with the buyer under every rule except DDP.
EXW, FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DPU and DDP work for air, road, rail, sea and multimodal moves, including containers. FCA, CPT and CIP are the right choice for most containerised and air cargo.
FAS, FOB, CFR and CIF are built around a ship’s rail. They suit bulk and breakbulk cargo. With containers, the box is handed over at a terminal days before loading, so FCA, CPT or CIP fit better.

What is the difference between FOB and FCA?

Under FOB the risk passes when the goods are on board the ship, which suits bulk cargo. Under FCA it passes when the goods are handed to the buyer’s carrier, for example at a CFS or ICD, which is what really happens with containers and air cargo.
Do Incoterms decide when ownership passes?
Does CIF give the buyer full insurance?
Not necessarily. CIF only requires minimum cover, Institute Cargo Clauses (C). Buyers who want all-risks cover should ask for it in the contract or buy extra cover. CIP requires all-risks cover.

What is the difference between HAZ, DG and general cargo?

HAZ (hazardous) and DG (dangerous goods) mean the same thing in shipping: goods with a UN number under the IMDG Code (sea) or the IATA / ICAO rules (air). General cargo is anything that is not DG. Some general cargo still needs special handling, such as perishables, valuables or out-of-gauge cargo.

Why do shipping lines ask for an MSDS even for non-DG cargo?

Lines, CFSs and airlines check chemicals, oils, powders and similar cargo to make sure nothing dangerous is misdeclared. Misdeclared cargo has caused serious ship fires, so most lines want the MSDS and a non-hazardous declaration on your letterhead.
